raw_response.printed_headline_estimate: Poisson Model 3 (fully adjusted, N = 4,218 villages; Table 1 p. 7, Table A1 p. 21, Appendix B p. 23, Appendix C p. 28): (1) Number of Community Action Planning (CAP) participants (log scale): beta = 0.19, PR = 1.21 (95% CI: 1.05-1.38, p = 0.007; crude Model 1 PR = 1.42, 95% CI: 1.24-1.63, p = 0.000; Logit OR = 1.82, 95% CI: 1.42-2.34, p = 0.000); (2) Tariffs > O&M costs (vs <= O&M ref): beta = 0.61, PR = 1.84 (95% CI: 1.70-2.01, p = 0.000; Logit OR = 6.90, 95% CI: 5.82-8.18, p = 0.000); (3) Village local revenue (PAD) per capita > Rp 30,000 (vs < Rp 5,000 ref): beta = 0.26, PR = 1.29 (95% CI: 1.16-1.44, p = 0.000).
raw_response.publication_year_note: Printed on PDF p. 1 as Volume 6 Issue 1 (2022), citation year 2022, and Available online: June 14, 2022 (Received: October 10, 2021; Accepted: November 29, 2021).
raw_response.rationale: This mixed-methods study includes a full inferential quantitative panel analysis (Poisson and Logit regressions across N = 4,218 PAMSIMAS Phase I villages in Indonesia; Table 1 p. 7, Table A1 p. 21, Appendix B p. 23, Appendix C pp. 26-28) predicting village-level water system sustainability/functionality (defined as consistently producing sufficient water for >80% of village beneficiaries across 5 consecutive years, 2014-2018, without rehabilitation—a Criterion 4 community water availability/reliability outcome). Both the focal participatory governance exposure—formal Community Action Planning (CAP) participation at project inception (Family B: PR = 1.21, 95% CI 1.05-1.38, p = 0.007)—and the co-estimated tariff cost-recovery rule—scheme tariffs exceeding O&M costs vs <= O&M costs (Family C: PR = 1.84, 95% CI 1.70-2.01, p = 0.000) and local fiscal revenue (PAD per capita > Rp 30,000: PR = 1.29, 95% CI 1.16-1.44, p = 0.000)—yield statistically significant inferential estimates with 95% CIs and p-values. Family B is assigned for the focal participatory planning exposure, with Family C tariff/fiscal effects also eligible and documented.
